I think they voting system in general is quite silly, arbitrary, and poorly conceived. However downvotes are a real issue that need to be dealt with. Three reasons:

1) http://cs.stanford.edu/people/jure/pubs/disqus-icwsm14.pdf - That is an academic study that actually quantified the results of downvotes across a variety of social media type systems and the results are surprising. It's incredibly counter intuitive but downvotes actually encourage people to post even more and continually lower quality posts. It also results in the downvoted individual tending to downvote other users which results in a sort of domino effect of shit posting.

2) This software relies exclusively on votes/time for the sorting and filtering comments. This obviously assumes that the more desirable content is, the more upvotes it gets. I think we can all mostly agree that this isn't really the case. Many people upvote comments even when they add little or nothing to the discussion or even are completely off topic. One that stood out to me recently was this. The thread was Elon Musk discussing his views on carbon emissions and the peculiarities of relying so heavily on a definitively finite resource. The most upvoted comment, by far, was that one liner anti-immigration post. The one that ended up at the top was no less inane. You have to scroll down to the bottom to actually find people starting to discuss what was actually said in the article. And this is pretty typical.

3) The whole voting system is completely open to trivial exploitation. The way content gets a lot of upvotes is by being seen by a large number of eyes. The way you get seen by a lot of eyes is getting a lot of upvotes. What this means is that a small number of people intentionally up or down voting a post early in its life can ultimately decide it's fate. Not a terrible bad thing when there's no bias (in the statistical sense) of the sample making that decision, but in reality there very often is.
